objectives: To assess the overall malignancy rate in patients with incidental solitary pulmonary nodules (SPNs) and conduct an in-depth analysis of potential risk factors, providing evidence-based guidance for clinical risk stratification and personalized follow-up and management strategies.
inclusion_criteria: Studies were included if they met the following criteria: (1) participants were patients with incidental SPNs, defined as rounded lesions �3c=3 cm in diameter detected via imaging without prior suspicion of malignancy; (2) exposure was incidental SPNs confirmed as malignant or pathologically diagnosed as lung cancer; (3) comparison was incidental SPNs confirmed as benign; (4) outcomes were the reported incidence of malignancy in incidental SPNs and associated risk factors; for a risk factor to be included in the meta-analysis, it had to be reported in at least three independent studies; malignancy required histopathological confirmation (via surgery or biopsy), while benign status was defined by either definitive histopathology, resolution or significant regression on follow-up imaging over at least 24 months, or characteristic benign calcification patterns confirmed by an experienced radiologist; studies that did not apply comparable rigorous verification standards were excluded; and (5) study design was observational.
exclusion_criteria: Exclusion criteria were: (1) non-incidental SPNs; (2) insufficient confirmation of diagnosis; (3) incomplete data; and (4) significant imaging limitations. In addition, studies that did not apply comparable rigorous verification standards for benign/malignant nodule classification were excluded.
